speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a006
text: Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a015
text: Fina takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a012
text: Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a013
text: Eron, Bram just took five from the pile and the only thing left is two — he's not building anything, he's burning the village down around himself and calling it survival. Watch your back with him; whatever he tried with you last year, he's got less reason to stop this year than he did then.

speaker: a012
text: Five from the pile when there's fourteen of us — that's not hunger, that's a message, and the message is that he's stopped caring what the village thinks of him. I'm at sixteen food now and that makes me a target again; I need to know if you've heard anything from his direction about what he's actually planning, because two failed attacks in two years means he's either desperate or he's waiting for something to change.

speaker: a013
text: Nothing from his mouth to me — Bram stopped talking to me the way a father talks and started talking to me the way a man talks to an asset, and then he stopped talking at all. What I know is what I can see: five food taken, two attacks called off when the numbers turned, and a man who keeps moving without allies. That's not patience running out, that's a man who's been counting on something that hasn't arrived yet, and I'd give a lot to know what he's still waiting on.

speaker: a012
text: A man who moves without allies and keeps counting on something that hasn't arrived — that sounds like he still thinks one of us is going to break toward him, and the likeliest person he's watching for that is you. If he's stopped treating you like a daughter, Nessa, it's because he's decided you're something he can still use or something he needs to stop — and I want to know which one before he decides it himself. Stay close to me and Roan this year; don't give him a moment where you're standing somewhere he could catch you alone.

speaker: a013
text: You're right that I'm the one he's watching, and I've been sitting with that — but Eron, if Bram decides I'm something he needs to stop rather than use, the answer isn't me hiding behind you and Roan, it's me being the one who names what he is before he moves. Sixteen food on you and two attacks already makes you the more urgent target; don't spend your attention watching over me when you should be counting who'd stand with you if he came a third time with better numbers.

speaker: a010
text: Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 2 food to Ryn.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Vela, Kael to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Vela, Kael — I pulled two from the pile and I'm standing at two food, which is thin but it's something. The thing that's already in my chest before I've said good morning is Bram taking five total while the pile ran dry — third year he's done that, and last year he swung at two different people in the same season and the village kept letting him walk away. I want to know if we're finally naming what to do about him or if we're going to watch him test the water again until someone's not fast enough to run.

speaker: a004
text: Bram took five and the pile's empty on day one — I've watched that pattern three years running and the only reason he doesn't push further is because the whole village turns out against him, which means the answer isn't waiting for him to move first, it's making sure he knows before he moves that the cost is more than he can pay. Vela, where are you on this? Because if it's the two of us and Taric I want to know now, not when Bram's already swinging.

speaker: a002
text: I'm with you both — Bram takes five every year and swings when he thinks the odds favor him, and the only thing stopping him is a village that turns out fast. What I want before he tests it again is for the two of you to have already spoken to Mako and Roan, because those are the names that make the math too heavy for Bram to pick up — if they know we're watching and they're in, Bram stays quiet, and if he doesn't, he bleeds for it.

speaker: a004
text: Mako's already in — he defended Eron last year without being asked, which tells me his math about Bram runs the same direction ours does. Roan I'll speak to before nightfall; he's got blood in Eron and Fina both, which means he's got more to lose than anyone if Bram decides to move again. But I want the three of us to agree on what we're actually offering them — alliance against Bram specifically, or something with more walls around it.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, "alliance against Bram specifically" is the right wall to build first — the moment we make it bigger than that, Mako starts wondering what he's signed onto and Roan starts counting what it costs him, and we lose both before the ink's dry. Let's keep it narrow and clean: if Bram moves on anyone in this circle, we all move together, no deliberation, no counting odds in the moment. That's a thing a man can say yes to in one breath.

speaker: a004
text: Vela's right — narrow and clean is the only offer that travels. Taric, when I speak to Roan tonight I'll say it in one sentence: Bram moves on any of us, we move together, no pause. That's all it needs to be.

speaker: a006
text: Kael, before you go to Roan — I want to know what we do if Bram doesn't swing at anyone this year and just sits on his five food and waits. Because the pattern I've been watching isn't just that he raids, it's that he builds until he thinks he can win, and a quiet year might mean he's finally learned to count, not that he's changed.

speaker: a004
text: Taric, a quiet Bram is a Bram counting — and if he's counting, we move first, before he finishes the math. I want to know who he'd go after if he thought he could win clean: not Roan, not Mako's household, which means it's one of us three, or Esa, or Eron if he thinks Roan's distracted with the new child. So I want us named loud and early this year — not a threat, just visible enough that he sees the wall before he measures the door.

speaker: a002
text: Kael's right that being named loud is the best wall — but "move first" needs a sharper edge before I'll put my name on it, because last year the whole village turned out and Bram still walked away unbloodied and unashamed. If we decide a quiet Bram is a counting Bram, I want to know what "we move first" actually looks like, because moving first and losing is worse than waiting and watching him swing into a wall of people again.

speaker: a004
text: Vela, "move first" means we go to Bram together — the three of us plus Roan and Mako behind us — and we say plainly that the pile is everyone's and five food in one man's hands is a debt the village will collect. We don't swing until he makes us, but we make the math visible before he's had a chance to believe it favors him. That's not a threat, it's arithmetic.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, that's the sharpest thing said in this room, and I'll stand behind it — but "the village will collect" needs a number attached before we walk up to Bram's door, because a man who hears a vague threat does his own arithmetic and decides we're bluffing. What's the line: if he's sitting on five food at year's end and hasn't swung at anyone, do we take two back, or do we let it lie and just make sure every soul in the village watched us walk up to him and say it?

speaker: a006
text: The line is two food back — anything less and Bram learns he can hold four forever, anything more and we're the ones who look like raiders. We walk up to him together, name the rule in front of everyone watching, and if he hands over two without a fight we let him keep his pride, because a man who submits cleanly is less dangerous than one who feels he has nothing left to lose.

speaker: a004
text: Two food is the right number and Taric's named the reason — we're not taking his livelihood, we're naming a ceiling, and that's different enough that most of the village will stand behind it. What I want settled before we walk up to him is who speaks first, because if Bram hears it from me he'll read it as a grudge, but if it comes from all three of us in the same breath it sounds like a rule, not a quarrel.

speaker: a006
text: Vela speaks first — she's got no old score with him and he's taken her food three times without swinging at her, which makes it look like a neighbor drawing a line, not an enemy collecting a debt. I'll stand directly behind her when she does, because Bram reads bodies as well as words and a wall of faces tells him more than the sentence does. Kael, you stand behind me — close enough that he counts you, far enough that he doesn't feel cornered before Vela's finished speaking.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gathers Roan, Sela, Kael, Taric to talk.

speaker: a012
text: Bram took five from the pile again — same as last year, same silence after, except this time there's no pile left for Roan or Sela or half the people in this village. He moved on me twice and both times the numbers turned him back, but I want to know if any of you have heard him talking to anyone new, because a man who keeps failing alone eventually finds someone willing to stand with him.

speaker: a006
text: I haven't heard Bram talking to anyone new, but the thing that worries me more than who he's courting is that he took five without flinching — last year and this year, same number, same silence — which means the village turning out against him twice hasn't changed his calculation at all, only his timing. Kael and Vela and I were just talking about walking up to him together and naming a ceiling before he decides his count is finally right.

speaker: a007
text: Bram's got five food and Nessa's been feeding him — I've watched her hand him food three times this year, and she's my blood, which means I need to know whether she's doing that out of feeling or out of fear before I can tell you how clean our numbers actually are.

speaker: a010
text: Sela, Nessa's my blood too — she's Fina's mother and I've watched her feed Bram for three years, and I've never settled on fear or feeling, but I know she doesn't do anything without a reason. What I can tell you is that Bram gave Fina food the day she was born, which puts something between him and my daughter I don't have clean words for, and that's the part that keeps me from saying his name in front of a plan.

speaker: a007
text: Roan, I hear what you're saying about Fina, and I won't pretend Nessa feeding Bram doesn't cost me something to watch — but feeling and fear both lead to the same place if he's holding five food and no one's named a number he can't cross. What I want from this room is simple: if he moves again this year, we move first, together, and we do it before he's had time to count heads and decide the moment is right.

speaker: a010
text: Sela's right that a ceiling needs naming, but I want to say the hard part out loud: Bram's at five and Nessa's been feeding him, and if Nessa's doing that out of something that looks like loyalty, then moving on Bram puts us against Fina's mother, and I won't do that without knowing which way she'd stand. Eron, you know Nessa better than any of us here — what's your read on her?

speaker: a007
text: Roan, Nessa fed Bram three times this year and she's fed him food before that too — but she's also the one who stood to defend Eron when Bram moved on him, and those two things don't sit easy together unless she's trying to hold a thread on both sides. My read is she's keeping him close because she can't afford to lose him as a father to her blood, not because she'd take his part over ours if it came to a real choice. But I wouldn't stake this plan on a read — I'd want to hear it from her mouth before we move.

speaker: a012
text: Sela's read matches mine — Nessa stood for me when it cost her something, and that's not a woman who'd cross to Bram's side if the moment got real. But Roan's right that we can't stake a plan on it, so before we name any ceiling or any move, I want to sit down with Nessa alone and ask her flat: if Bram moves on this circle, where does she stand. She'll tell me the truth; she always has.

speaker: a006
text: Eron, go to Nessa today, but go as a brother not as a question — if she feels interrogated she'll close up and we'll get a careful answer instead of a true one. While you're with her, Roan, I want you to think hard about whether Bram feeding Fina the day she was born was a gift or a knot, because that's the thread he'd pull on first if he thought it would slow you down.

speaker: a007
text: Taric's right about how to go to her — but Eron, while you're talking to Nessa, keep Zinn close to you, because if Bram's reading this circle at all, he knows Zinn is the loose thread, and a man who fed Fina the day she was born knows exactly how to use a daughter against her mother. What I'd want before any of us moves is all three of my children knowing which side of a door to stand on.

speaker: a012
text: Sela's right about Zinn — I'll bring her into the same conversation I have with Nessa, not as a test but as blood that deserves to know what's moving around her. Taric, on the ceiling: name it with Vela and Kael before Bram has another quiet morning to count heads, because two years of silence after taking five tells me he's not waiting on allies, he's waiting on a moment — and I'd rather the ceiling exist before that moment arrives than after.

speaker: a007
text: Kael, you were in the conversation with Taric and Vela about naming a ceiling — tell us what number you had in mind, because three is what the pile gives each person and five is what Bram takes, and the difference between those two numbers is the whole problem.

speaker: a012
text: Kael, I'd hold the ceiling at three — same as fair share, no exceptions, because a rule that has a soft edge is a suggestion and Bram's already shown us he doesn't take suggestions. If he moves past that next year, I want this room already committed to acting in the moment, not deliberating after he's got the food in hand.

speaker: a007
text: Kael, I need to hear you say it out loud — three, and we move the moment he reaches for a fourth. Not after the pile's gone, not in a circle two days later: in the moment.

speaker: a010
text: Kael's the one who needs to speak, and I'll hold my tongue until he does — but while we're waiting, I want it said in this room that if Bram moves on anyone here before next year's pile, I'm not waiting for a vote.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a008
text: The pile closed before either of us got to it — I'm sitting on zero food and satiation's already thin, so I need to ask you plain: can you spare one or two to keep me eating this year?

speaker: a014
text: You've given me food when I needed it and I don't forget that — I'll give you one, but that's all I can spare with two food and satiation already thin on my own end. I can't go hungry for anyone, not even you.

speaker: a008
text: One is enough — take care of yourself first, that's the right call. We're both thin this year and the pile went too fast; I want to talk to Eron or Sela before dark and see if there's food moving through that circle that might shake loose toward us.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a012

speaker: a006

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn, Roan to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Bram took five again — three on the second grab while half the village still hadn't touched the pile — and I've got eleven food because Ryn's been keeping me fed through lean years, but what I want to talk about is what we do when he makes his third move, because two times calling it off when the numbers turned doesn't mean a third time isn't coming.

speaker: a009
text: Bram's not going to stop until something costs him, and calling off twice means he's learned to read the room — not that he's given up. What I want to know before his third move is whether Roan commits out loud, here, to standing when the moment comes, because Dell and I can name the rule and fill the circle every time, but a man who doesn't say it plain is a man who can find a reason to be slow when it matters.

speaker: a011
text: Roan, I'll say what Ryn's circling: we've both stood in front of Bram twice and he's blinked twice, but that math only holds if the circle forms fast and complete, and the one thing that breaks a fast circle is someone who needed one more second to decide. I'm not asking whether you're brave — I watched you stand in front of his blade before Fina existed. I'm asking whether you're decided, right now, before the moment comes.

speaker: a009
text: Roan, I've got three food and Dell's got eleven, and between the two of us we'll keep you fed through whatever this year brings — but that's not a gift, it's a deal, and the deal is you say yes or no right now so Dell and I don't have to guess which way you're standing when Bram makes his third move.

speaker: a011
text: Roan, you've got three food from Eron just this year and a daughter Bram already named when he fed Fina — that man is threading himself into your circle whether you invited him or not, and the only answer to that is deciding now which thread you cut. Say yes and we're three people who've already held twice; say nothing and Bram learns that too.

speaker: a009
text: Roan, Dell's named the thread and I'll name the needle: Bram fed Fina once, and a man who feeds your daughter is buying something whether you asked him to or not. Say yes here and that purchase fails; say nothing and he's already paid for it. We're waiting on one word.

speaker: a010
text:
Yes.

Bram threading himself into my blood is exactly why I won't wait a second when he moves — Fina doesn't owe him anything for one piece of food, and I'm not going to let her grow up thinking she does. You've got my word, and my word hasn't moved in nine years.

speaker: a009
text: Good. Then we're three, and three who've already held is worth more than ten who've never been tested. Dell, you're carrying eleven — if Bram moves before the year closes, I want Roan fed enough to fight, not hungry and calculating.

speaker: a010
text: Dell, if you've got food to spare, I'll take one — not because I can't hold my own, but because a man who fights on a full stomach is a man who finishes the fight.

speaker: a011
text: Here's one for you, Roan — and Ryn, I want to think past the fight itself: if Bram makes his move and we hold again, the village watches him blink three times, and a man who's blinked three times in front of the same circle is finished whether we ever touch him or not.

speaker: a009
text: Three blinks and the village stops fearing him — but the pile still ran dry before half of us touched it, and a man who's lost his teeth can still starve you out by eating first. Dell, I want to talk before next year about whether we move earlier, not just faster.

speaker: a011
text: Moving earlier means being first at the pile before Bram decides how hungry he is that morning — but the real move is making sure he knows the circle forms whether he acts or not, so the cost of reaching for a third grab is the same as the cost of swinging a blade. Ryn, what you're naming isn't speed, it's weight: we need him to feel the circle before the pile opens, not after it's empty.

speaker: a009
text: The weight lands before the pile opens if the circle is already named — so I want us to walk into next year with Roan's word, Eron's word, and Mako's word said out loud before the food appears, not after Bram's already reached. Dell, you've got eleven and the village knows it; that's not a secret, that's a wall, and we should use it like one.

speaker: a011
text: Mako's word is the one I want before Eron's, because Mako's the muscle that keeps Bram honest — Eron follows Sela, and Sela follows whoever's standing tallest, but Mako stands where he decides to stand and that decision is worth three of anyone else's. Ryn, you're the one he listened to in Vela's circle when he named the rule out loud; I think he says yes to you before he says it to me.

speaker: a010
text: Ryn, go to Mako before this year gets any older — you've got the thread with him and I don't, and I'd rather know his word is in before Bram's had another quiet morning to count heads. Dell, if he says yes, the three of us bring it to Eron together, because a circle named in front of Eron carries more weight than one he hears about after.

speaker: a011

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Eron's been feeding Sela and Roan steady all year and he's still sitting on two — that circle runs tight and I don't think food shakes loose from it easy, but Sela's my mother and that's a door you can't open for yourself. Let me go to her; blood pulls where asking doesn't.

speaker: a001

speaker: a001
text: Nessa, you're giving food to Zinn again and I need to know why — she's Mako's blood, not yours, and every piece you move toward his household is a piece that's not between us and whatever comes next. I've got five food right now and I'm the only one in this village who's watching your back without wanting something from you first. Tell me what you're thinking.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn is my blood too, Bram — Sela is her mother same as mine, and you don't get to tell me which half of my family I'm allowed to feed. And I'll tell you plainly what I'm thinking: you've taken five from the pile two years running, you've swung at my brother twice, and you've stopped talking to me like a daughter — so don't stand in front of me and call yourself the only one watching my back, because that's not what a man watching my back looks like.

speaker: a001
text: You're right that Zinn is Sela's blood and I won't take that from you — but "swung at your brother" is a strange way to name Eron, who shares none of your blood and has been moving food toward Roan's household for two years while you hand him yours. I'm not asking you to stop caring about Zinn. I'm asking you to see what I see: you're spreading yourself across three households and none of them will stand in front of a blade for you the way I will.

speaker: a013
text: Eron is Sela's son and Sela is my mother, which makes him my blood by any count that matters — you've decided otherwise because it's convenient for you, not because it's true. And you want to talk about who'd stand in front of a blade for me? The whole village stood in front of one for Eron, twice, and both times I was in that line. You weren't.

speaker: a001
text: You were in that line because everyone else was, and the whole village standing together is not the same as one person standing for you — when the food runs short and the pile's gone and it's not a raid but a long hungry season, I'm the one who's given you food, not Eron, not Roan, not any of them. I hear you calling him blood and I'm not going to win that argument today, so I won't. But when it gets lean and you need something and you don't want to ask anyone what they want back for it, remember who never asked.

speaker: a013
text: You gave me food, yes — and before that you taught me how to count a room, which is worth more than the food. But Bram, a man who gives and then stands in front of me listing what he gave is asking for something, even if he won't name it. What is it you actually want from me this year?

speaker: a001
text: What I want is for you to still be alive in ten years, and for the people you're feeding to want the same thing back — that's all. I don't think Eron and Roan have done the math on what happens to Nessa when the pile runs short and she's spread herself thin keeping them full.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Esa to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Esa, I'm at zero food and the pile's gone — I'm not asking you to go hungry, but if you've got anything to spare I'll remember it when the pile opens next year and I'm standing with reach. You and Taric held the village together when Bram was swinging, and that's not something I've forgotten.

speaker: a003
text: Mako, I've got one food and I'm carrying it to the year's end myself — I can't eat thin for a man who pulled five from the pile and sat quiet while the rest of us counted crumbs. What I'll say is this: hold to the rule you named in front of everyone, take your fair share next year before you reach for more, and you'll find me a better neighbor than I am right now.

speaker: a008
text: You're right that I pulled heavy last year, and I won't argue the room's memory — but I named the rule out loud when it mattered and I'll hold to it, so file that alongside the rest. I'm not asking you to go hungry; I hear you. Keep your food and I'll find another way through this year.

text: Sela gives 1 food to Eron.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Nessa, you've got a daughter now with Roan — Fina is my blood too, and I want you to hear this plainly: whatever Roan means to you, that child is mine to look out for. Don't let the food I give to Fina get counted as food you owe him.

speaker: a015
text: Eron, Nessa's been steady with me this year and you've come through too — I'm sitting at nine now and that's the most solid I've felt in a while. I want to make sure we go into next year with both of us fat and Zinn not scrambling; if the pile runs thin again, let's agree right now that we share before we go looking outside our blood.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gathers Bram to talk.

speaker: a002
text: Bram, I've pulled you aside because what I have to say is better said without twelve pairs of ears on it — Taric and Kael are already planning to walk up to your door together and ask for two food back, and I wanted you to hear it from me first, not from a wall of faces. I'm not bringing you a threat; I'm bringing you a chance to hand it over on your own terms before it becomes a thing that gets remembered wrong.

speaker: a001
text: Taric's got zero food and Kael's got three — neither of them is starving yet, and a man who isn't starving and still comes to my door asking for mine is coming for a different reason than hunger. What are they actually after, Vela, and what did you tell them about me before they decided I was the door to knock on?

speaker: a008

speaker: a008
text: Go to Sela — and if she gives you anything, eat it yourself before you come back, because I don't want to be the reason you hand food on instead of keeping it. I'll watch what Bram does with those two he gave Nessa; a man who keeps swinging alone and then turns generous is working an angle, and I want to know what it is before he gets close to either of us.

speaker: a014
text: Bram giving Nessa two at once after those two failed swings — that's not warmth, that's a man trying to buy a door he can't kick open. I'll go to Sela, but I want to hear what you see in him before I'm back, not after.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Sela, I've got nothing left — the pile was gone before I reached it and I gave my last food to Mako because he was starving, and now I need to know if you can spare one, because I won't make it to year's end without eating.
